page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.6xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, this instance features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 12 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The hardware profile includes 48.0 GB of total RAM, allocating 2.0 GB per vCPU. Architectural extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI support, AES acceleration, FMA, and BMI2 instructions. It provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps, with zero local storage bundled and no dedicated GPU hardware.

In empirical performance tests, the instance demonstrates balanced multi-threaded capabilities alongside modest single-thread execution. Benchmark metrics highlight weak single-core stress-ng performance and single-threaded gzip compression rate, both landing in the bottom 25th percentile. Conversely, multi-core CPU workloads achieve average results across Geekbench, PassMark, and stress-ng tests. Memory operations maintain steady throughput, recording uncached read speeds of 108.94 GB/sec and write speeds of 47.99 GB/sec. Redis SET operations reach 20.09 million operations per second, while static web serving achieves 15.86 GB/sec throughput.

The resource ratio of 2 vCPUs per 1 GB of RAM underscores its design for compute-bound tasks that do not demand extensive memory footprints. While the lack of local SSD storage requires attachment to external cloud block storage, the 8 Gbps network bandwidth provides reasonable throughput for distributed cluster communication. The configuration yields cost-efficient resource density for parallel execution workloads, software compilation via Clang, multi-threaded batch processing, and high-concurrency web serving fleets.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.6xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance equipped with 24 dedicated vCPUs and 48.0 GB of memory, delivering a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz on x86_64 architecture, the instance incorporates 12 physical cores with hyperthreading and instruction set extensions including AVX-512 VNNI and AES. It provides an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without included local storage or dedicated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations indicate modest single-core throughput, balanced by solid average multi-core CPU, memory bandwidth, and static web serving capabilities. The configuration offers cost-effective execution density for compute-bound parallel workloads, multi-threaded batch processing, software build pipelines, and high-concurrency web serving applications requiring consistent vCPU allocation without extensive per-core memory requirements.
